title: A card folder that cannot be read vanishes from the listing, and the card is then 'Safe to format'
what: list_card swallows OSError from scandir of a folder and from an entry stat, so an unreadable folder's files are absent from `files`; the field verdict judges only what was listed and nothing marks the listing partial.
cost: Flaky card: DCIM/101MEDIA throws EIO, 100MEDIA files are at home -> 'Safe to format: all 3 files are at home'; 101MEDIA footage has no copy and is formatted away. The copy run copies the same short list, so lanes are green too.
evidence: probe_unreadable.py: scandir raises for 101MEDIA -> 3 of 6 files listed -> verdict safe, safeToFormat=True.
fix: list_card returns an `unreadable` list like LedgerScan; card_verdict refuses safeToFormat (state 'incomplete', naming the folder) while it is non-empty; copy run reports it.

title: 'Safe to format' ignores originals whose extension is not on an allow-list (Nikon N-RAW .NEV and others)
what: is_judged is an allow-list (MASTER/AUDIO/MEDIA exts + extras); .NEV, .ARX, .cine, .CRW, .ERF, .RWL, .M2T, .MOD, .VOB are not judged (fail-open) and FieldCopier._record drops them.
cost: Nikon card with N-RAW video + stills: 'Safe to format' once the stills have two copies, whatever happened to the .NEV clips; an N-RAW-only card reads 'Nothing on this card needs backing up'.
evidence: Inline probe: is_judged False for .NEV/.ARX/.cine/.CRW/.ERF/.M2T/.MOD/.VOB/.RWL; card_verdict of one 5 GB .NEV -> state empty, 'Nothing on this card needs backing up'.
fix: Judge every file except a deny-list (sidecars, thumbnails, proxies, system/temp, ._ twins); add the missing exts to the ledger rules separately.

title: The verdict rewrites field-local-copies.jsonl with fsync once per file after a sync: 28 s for a 2,000-file card
what: LedgerView._raw calls LocalCopies.forget per lookup that the mirror now covers; forget rewrites the whole jsonl + fsync. One rewrite per file, inside the page's state request; overlapping 4 s polls start more verdicts. add() is quadratic too.
cost: First verdict per card after each delivering sync: 500 files 10.6 s, 2,000 files 28.0 s page stall + fsync storm; at the 60k-row cap ~18 MB per rewrite, ~36 GB written for a 2,000-file card (estimated).
evidence: probe_verdict.py: F=500 cover -> 10.60 s; F=2000 cover -> 28.01 s; local rows 4000 -> 0.
fix: Collect covered rows and forget once per verdict (or reconcile on the sync thread after a pull); index LocalCopies by (name_lc,size) and (volume_id,path).

title: Every verdict reopens SQLite per file, re-reads field-state.json six times per file and scans all local copies per file: 4.4 s per 2,000-file card every 20 s
what: Per judged file: one SQLite connect + PRAGMA + executescript(SCHEMA), ~6 FieldStore file reads+parses via KindResolver, a linear LocalCopies scan; at home each NAS copy is stat'ed over SMB. Lane planning repeats the per-file lookups.
cost: Page polls 4 s idle / 1 s copying, verdict TTL 20 s and invalidated by lane ends/syncs. 2,000 files: 4.4 s (1.8 s SQLite, 1.1 s LocalCopies scan, 0.67 s for 12,000 state-file reads); +~6 s at 20k local rows (estimated); +2-6 s SMB stats at home (estimated).
evidence: probe_verdict.py F=2000: 4.42 s, field-state.json reads=12000, sqlite connects=2000; cProfile breakdown.
fix: One connection (or one json_each batch query) per verdict, schema once per process, kinds/guesses/info snapshotted per verdict, indexed LocalCopies, pool presence cached per verdict.

title: Cards in fixed readers (CFexpress B) are reported to the sorter but cannot be copied by the companion or the field page
what: 7ac37ed made sorter_cards report fixed-disk cards; card_copy._find_card/_card_gone, field_service._cards_from and field_copy._card_present still look only at removable volumes.
cost: Every sorter card-ingest of a CFexpress B / BMCC SSD card fails non-retryably ('not in a card reader on this computer'); the field page cannot back it up and offers it as a destination (kind unknown).
evidence: Code read; git show --stat 7ac37ed touched sorter_cards only.
fix: One shared 'is this volume a card' predicate (removable, or fixed with a camera layout) used by card_copy, field_service and field_copy; exclude such volumes from destinations.

title: The ledger outbox is quadratic to flush and fully re-parsed on every field-page poll
what: Each 500-copy batch re-reads the file twice, re-serialises every line with sort_keys and rewrites + fsyncs it; pending() parses the whole file per page poll and per flusher tick (no backoff on transport errors).
cost: Measured flush (network excluded): 10k 1.0 s, 40k 20.9 s, 80k 73.6 s; 200k cap ~7-8 min and ~11 GB written (extrapolated). pending() 0.26 s at 80k on every 1 s poll during a copy.
fix: Send from one read with a sent-offset, drop delivered lines in one rewrite at the end (or a SQLite outbox), cache pending() by size+mtime; keep 'nothing deleted before a 200' and the rejected file.

title: The mirror is keyed on the volumes plugged in now: every card in or out re-pulls everything (NAS included) and deletes away drives' copies
what: sync() pulls for the current attachment set (cards included); a different set resets the cursor to '' and _forget_other_volumes deletes rows of unplugged drives; _root_by_vid keeps an unplugged drive's letter so _present drops its copies. Both contradict 'a copy on a drive that is away is believed'.
cost: Each card insert re-downloads all rows incl. nas:... (estimated 10^5-10^6 rows, 20-200 pages over Tailscale, tens-hundreds of MB). Card copied to D1 and D2, D1 bagged, next card in, sync -> first card falls to one copy and is re-copied.
evidence: Code read: `same = meta volumes == want`, else cursor '' and _forget_other_volumes(ids).
fix: Pull for a persistent growing set (volumes ever recorded + pool), cursor per volume, never forget on unplug; drop stale _root_by_vid entries each scan.

title: Physical-disk key cached by drive letter for the process lifetime: two partitions of one disk can count as two copies
what: _lane_key caches physical_key(root) by root path forever; letters and device numbers are reassigned while the companion runs for weeks, and the stale key is persisted into LocalCopies rows' phys.
cost: E: was disk:3; today a two-partition SSD (disk:2) is E: and F:, both 'ours' -> keys disk:3 and disk:2 -> two counted copies on one physical disk -> 'Safe to format'. Also parallel lanes onto one disk.
evidence: Code read against file_verdict's promise that two partitions of one disk never make two.
ledger: new (regression of the 2026-11-10 review's physical-disk rule)
fix: Re-ask the IOCTL per scan or key the cache by serial+letter and drop absent volumes.

title: A removable volume holding footage is re-listed in full and re-posted every 10 s whenever its free space moves
what: The relist signature includes free bytes; a volume being written to is re-walked each tick (reading every .xml head and .wav header) and its whole listing POSTed. A removable field drive with a recorder/BMCC backup (media at depth 2) is a 'generic' card.
cost: 20k files: 0.8-1.2 s per list on NVMe (slower on USB HDD, competing with the copy), 6 re-lists/min, 1.8 MB body each; idle every 300 s. Field page re-lists at its 4 s poll.
evidence: probe_listcard.py: list_card 0.80 s, 20005 files, 2000 xml reads, 1.8 MB body; one minute of ticks while written -> 6 full re-lists, 5.1 s.
fix: Leave free out of the relist signature (root+capacity+root mtime), skip running copies' destinations, gzip the cards POST.

title: The Python copier's 'read back in full' verify reads the OS page cache, not the media
what: verify_whole re-reads the partial right after writing it with a plain buffered open; the pages are still cached, so the hash checks memory, not what reached the drive.
cost: Every Python-copier copy (Macs, PCs without TeraCopy) is recorded verified 'full' without proving the medium; a corrupting USB bridge yields copies that count toward 'safe to format'.
evidence: Code read; no FILE_FLAG_NO_BUFFERING / F_NOCACHE / fadvise in the module.
fix: Verify with an uncached read (Windows FILE_FLAG_NO_BUFFERING, macOS F_NOCACHE, Linux fadvise DONTNEED after fsync); keep the hash-while-copying pass.

title: TeraCopy's wait spawns tasklist every 5 s per lane for the whole copy
what: wait_for_job calls _is_running (a tasklist subprocess) on every poll even while the history DB says the job is running.
cost: 186 ms per tasklist measured; 3 lanes x 1 h = 2,160 spawns, ~6.7 min of process time beside the copy.
evidence: Measure-Command over 5 tasklist runs: 186 ms each.
fix: Check the process only when the record is missing/locked or copied without verify; or enumerate processes via ctypes.

title: Every lane reads the whole card on its own; three destinations read the card three times at once
what: One CardJob per lane group, all concurrent, each reading every source file; on the Python path a single read + hash could fan out to N writers.
cost: 256 GB card to 3 drives = 768 GB read in three interleaved streams from one reader (estimated 1.5-3x slower when the reader is the bottleneck). TeraCopy path cannot share a read.
fix: Fan-out copy for the Python copier (one read/hash, N partial writers, each verified); a failed writer drops out without stopping the read.

title: Proxy-by-name rule has drifted from the ledger's, and the field page never uses the server's rules
what: field_mode uses `S03\.mp4$` and the built-in Rules copy; the ledger uses `\dS\d{2}\.mp4$` and its own rules_doc, so the two disagree and server-side rule changes never reach the page.
cost: C0001S01.MP4 is a proxy to the ledger, a master to the page (extra 'short' files, safe direction); future server-side exts missed by the page.
fix: Cache the server's rules_doc with the mirror pull and build field_mode's Rules from it, one shared proxy regex.
